en: For beauty, for divinity, the image lacked life; the divine in the community of love, this life, lacked image and shape.

But in the risen one, and then in the one exalted to heaven, the image found life again and love the presentation of its unity; in this remarriage of spirit and body the opposition of the living and the dead has disappeared and has united itself in one God; the longing of love has found itself as living being and can now enjoy itself, whose veneration is now the religion of the congregation; the need of religion finds its satisfaction in this risen Jesus, in this configured love.

The contemplation of the resurrection of Jesus as an event is the viewpoint of the historian, who has nothing to do with religion; faith or unbelief in it, as mere actuality without the interest of religion, is a matter of the understanding, whose activity, the fixation of objectivity, is precisely the death of religion, and to appeal to it means to abstract from religion.

But of course the understanding seems to have a right to speak too, since the objective side of God is not merely a shape of love, but exists for itself and, as an actuality in the world of actualities, claims a place.

And therefore it is difficult to hold fast the religious side of the risen Jesus, the configured love in its beauty; for only through an apotheosis has he become God, his divinity is a deification of one who is also present as actual; he had lived as a human individual, had died on the cross and been buried.

This blemish of humanity is something quite different from the shape that is proper to God; the objective in God, his shape, is objective only to the extent that it is only the presentation of the love uniting the congregation, only the pure opposition of it, and contains nothing that is not itself in love, but here only as something opposed, nothing that would not at the same time be feeling.

But in this way there comes to the image of the risen one, to the union that has become essence, yet other attendant matter, fully objective, individual, which is to be paired with love, but as individual, as opposed, is to remain fixed, fixed for the understanding, whereby it is an actuality that always hangs on the deified one like lead on his feet, which pulls him down to earth; whereas [after all] the God should hover in the middle between heavenly infinity, boundlessness, and the earth, this gathering of pure limitations.
It cannot be got out of the soul, this twofoldness of the natures.

Just as Hercules through the funeral pyre, so too the deified one has raised himself up to hero only through a grave; but there the altars are consecrated to configured bravery, to the hero who has become God alone, no longer fighting or serving, while here [by contrast] not to the hero alone are the altars consecrated and the prayers brought; not the risen one alone is the salvation of sinners and the rapture of their faith; the teaching and wandering one and the one hanging on the cross is also worshiped.
It is this monstrous combination over which for so many centuries millions of God-seeking souls have struggled and tormented themselves.
zh: 对美、对神性来说，这形象缺少生命；而爱之共同体里的神性，这生命，缺少形象和形态。
但在复活者身上，随后又在升天者身上，形象重新找到了生命，爱也找到了它自身统一的呈现；在精神与肉体的这次再婚中，活者与死者的对立消失了，并在一个上帝里面结合起来；爱的渴望找到了自身作为活生生的本质，如今能够享受自身，而对它的崇敬如今就是教团的宗教；宗教的需要在这个复活的耶稣身上、在这种有形态的爱里得到了满足。
把耶稣的复活当作一桩事件来考察，是历史研究者的视角，他与宗教毫不相干；对它的信或不信，作为没有宗教关切的单纯现实性，是知性的事，而知性的活动，即对客观性的固定，恰恰就是宗教的死亡，求助于它就意味着抽掉宗教。
但知性当然似乎有权一起说话，因为上帝的客观方面并不只是一个爱的形态，而是自为地存在，并且作为诸现实性世界中的一种现实性占据一个位置。
因此，要把复活的耶稣的宗教方面、把有形态的爱在其美中紧紧抓住，是很困难的；因为他只是通过一次神化才成为上帝，他的神性是对一个同样作为现实者而现成存在的东西的神化；他曾作为一个人格的个体活过，死在十字架上并被埋葬。
这人性的污点与上帝本有的形态完全是另一回事；上帝的客观东西、他的形态，只是就以下程度才是客观的：它只是把那使教团结合起来的爱的呈现，只是这爱的纯粹对立，并且不包含任何不是本身就在爱里、只是在这里仅仅作为被对立者而存在的东西，不包含任何不同时是感受的东西。
但这样一来，在复活者的形象上，在这已成为本质的结合上，又加上了别的附属物，完全客观的、个体的东西，它要与爱配在一起，但作为个体的、作为被对立的东西却应当固定下来，为了知性而固定下来，它由此是一种现实性，总像铅一样挂在被神化者脚上，把他往地上拽；而[毕竟]上帝本应悬浮在天上的无限、无限制与大地——这纯然种种限制的聚集——之间。
它无法从灵魂里去掉，这双重本性。
正如赫拉克勒斯通过火葬的柴堆，被神化者也只是通过一座坟墓才把自己提升为英雄；但在那里，献祭的祭坛是给有形态的勇敢，[是]只给那已变成神、不再战斗也不再服役的英雄，而这里[相反]不是只给英雄才献上祭坛、献上祈祷；不是只有复活者才是罪人的得救和他们信仰的狂喜；那教导着、行走着的人，那挂在十字架上的人，也受到崇拜。
正是这个骇人的联结，多少世纪以来千百万寻求上帝的魂灵为它苦斗、为它受尽折磨。

en: It is not the servant form, not humiliation itself, as the covering of the divine, at which the drive for religion would take offense, if actuality contented itself with being a covering and passing away; but instead it is supposed to belong firmly and enduringly, on and in the God, to his essence, and individuality is to be the object of adoration; and the covering of actuality stripped off in the grave has risen up again out of the grave and has attached itself to the one risen as God.
This sad need of the congregation for an actual thing is deeply connected with its spirit and its fate.

Its love, which brought every form of life to consciousness as an object and thus despised it, had indeed recognized itself as configured in the risen one; but he was not merely love for it; for since its love, cut off from the world, did not present itself in the development of life, nor in its beautiful relations and in the cultivation of natural relations, since love was to be love and not to live, some criterion of the knowledge of it had to be present for the possibility of mutual faith in it.

Because love itself did not establish the thoroughgoing union, another bond was needed that linked the congregation and in which it at the same time found the certainty of the love of all; it had to recognize itself in an actuality.
This was now the sameness of faith, the sameness of having received a doctrine, of having a common master and teacher.
This is a distinguishing side of the spirit of the congregation, that the divine, that which unites it, has for it the form of something given.
To the spirit, to life, nothing is given; what it has received, that it has itself become, that has passed over into it in such a way that it is now a modification of the same, that it is its life.

But in the lifelessness of the love of the congregation the spirit of its love remained so poor, felt itself so empty, that it could not recognize the spirit that addressed it as full in itself, not as living in itself, and remained foreign to it.

A linkage with a foreign spirit, and one felt as foreign, is consciousness of dependence on it; since the love of the congregation on the one hand had overleaped itself, in that it extended itself over a whole assembly of human beings, and therefore on the other hand indeed became full in ideal content, but lost in life, the unfulfilled ideal of love was a positive for it, it recognized it as opposed to itself and [itself] as dependent on it; in its spirit lay the consciousness of discipleship and of a lord and master; its spirit was not completely presented in the configured love; the side of it, of having received and of learning and of standing lower than the master, found its presentation only in the shape of love, when with this there was at the same time linked an actuality that stood over against the congregation.

This higher opposed thing is not the sublimity of God, which the latter necessarily has, because in him the single individual does not recognize [himself] as equal to him, but rather in him the whole spirit of the united all is contained — rather it is a positive, objective thing, which has as much of the foreign, of lordship, in itself as there is dependence in the spirit of the congregation.

In this community of dependence, of being through a founder, in this admixture of something historical, actual into its life, the congregation recognized its real bond, the security of the union, which in lifeless love could not come to feeling.
zh: 如果现实性满足于充当外壳并转瞬即逝，那么宗教的冲动所抵触的，就并不是仆人的形态、并不是这屈辱本身——作为神性的外壳；但它却应当牢固而持久地、在被神化者身上并在他之中属于他的本质，个体性应当成为崇拜的对象；而那条在坟墓里被脱下的现实性的外壳，又从坟墓里升了起来，并附到了那作为上帝而复活的人身上。
教团这种对一个现实者的可悲需要，与它的精神及其命运深深相连。
它的爱把每一种生命形态都带进对一个对象的意识，并由此鄙视它们，这种爱在复活者身上固然认识到了自身作为有形态者；但对他们来说，他并不只是爱；因为它的爱既然与世界隔绝，就既没有在生命的发展中、也没有在生命美好的关系和对自然关系的培育中呈现出来，既然爱应当只是爱而不应当生活，那么为了彼此相信这爱成为可能，就必须有某个认识它的标准现成存在。
因为爱本身并没有建立起贯穿一切的结合，所以就需要另一条纽带把教团联结起来，而教团在其中同时找到所有人爱它的确定性；它必须在一个现实性上认识自身。
这现在就是信仰的相同，就是接受了同一种教导、拥有一位共同的师傅和教师的相同。
教团精神的一个突出方面就在于：那神性的东西、那把它结合起来的东西，对它来说具有一种被给予之物的形式。
对精神、对生命，没有什么东西是被给予的；它接受过的东西，它自己已经变成了，它已经如此转入它之中，以致它现在是它的一个变状，以致它就是它的生命。
但在教团之爱的无生命中，它的爱的精神始终如此贫乏，感到自己如此空虚，以致它无法把这向它说话的精神完满地认识为在自身之中、在自身之中活着的，并始终对它保持陌生。

与一个陌生的、并被感觉为陌生的精神的联结，就是对它的依赖意识；既然教团的爱一方面跳过了自身，因为它把自己扩展到一整群人的聚会上，因此另一方面在理想的内容上固然变得充实，在生命上却有所丧失，那么爱的未实现的理想对它来说就是一个肯定物，它把它认作与自身相对立，并认[自身]为依赖于它；在它的精神里有着门徒身份以及一位主和师傅的意识；它的精神在有形态的爱中并未得到完整的呈现；它的那个方面，即接受过、学习过并比师傅站得更低的方面，只有在爱的形态中才得到呈现，只要与这爱同时联结着一个与教团相对而立的现实性。
这个更高的对立物并不是上帝的崇高，后者必然具有这种崇高，因为在它之中单个的个人并不认[自身]为与它相等，而是在它之中包含了联合起来的一切人的整个精神——相反，它是一个肯定物、客观物，它在自身中包含多少陌生的东西、多少统治，教团的精神中就有多少依赖。
在这种依赖的共同体中，在这种通过一位创始者而存在的共同体中，在这种把某种历史性的、现实的东西混入其生命的状态中，教团认识到了它现实的纽带，即结合的确定性，而这在无生命的爱里是无法达到感受的。

en: This is the point at which the congregation, which in the love that keeps itself unmixed, outside all covenant with the world, seemed to have escaped all fate, was seized by it, but by a fate whose center was the extension of the love that flees all relations to a congregation, a fate that partly developed itself all the more in the very extension of the congregation, and partly, through this extension, increasingly coincided with the fate of the world, both in that it unconsciously took up many sides of it into itself, and in that it struggled against it and increasingly defiled itself.
zh: 这就是那个点：教团在那种保持自身不混杂、处在与世界的一切盟约之外的爱的里面，似乎已经躲过了一切命运，却在这里被命运抓住了，不过是被这样一种命运抓住，它的中心是把那逃避一切关系的爱扩展到教团之上，这命运一方面在教团自身的扩展中愈发发展起来，另一方面又由于这种扩展而越来越与世界的命运碰在一起，既不知不觉地把它的许多方面纳入自身，又因为它而与它斗争，并使自己越来越受污染。

en: The ungodly objective thing, for which adoration is also demanded, will never become a divine thing through all the splendor that shines around it.
zh: 那个非神性的客观东西，对它也要求崇拜，但无论有多少光辉环绕着它，它永远不会成为一个神性的东西。

en: To be sure, heavenly appearances surround the human Jesus too; higher beings are occupied with his birth; he himself is once transfigured into a radiant figure of light.
But even these forms of the heavenly are only outside the actual, and the more divine beings around the individual only serve to make the contrast stand out all the more.

Even less than such a passing nimbus can the activities that are regarded as divine and come out of him himself raise him into the higher shape; the miracles that do not merely hover around him but proceed from his inner power seem attributes worthy of a God, to characterize a God, in them the divine seems most intimately united with the objective and thus the harsh opposition and mere linkage of opposed things seems here to fall away; those wondrous workings the human being performs, he and the divine seem inseparable.
But the closer the linkage is, which nevertheless does not become a union, the more harshly the unnaturalness of the linked opposed things strikes one.
zh: 诚然，天上的现象也围绕着这个叫耶稣的人；更高的存在者忙着他的诞生；他自己也一度被变形为一道放光的光的形态。
但这些天上之物的形式也只在现实者之外，而围绕这个个体的那些更神圣的存在者，只是使这反差更加触目。
比这种转瞬即逝的光晕更不如的，是那些被视为神性、并从他自己里面出来的活动，它们更不能把他提升到更高的形态里去；那些不只是绕着他飘、而是从他的内在力量中产生出来的奇迹，看来像是配得上一个上帝的属性，像在刻画一个上帝，在它们里面，神性的东西似乎与客观的东西最内在地结合了，因而在这里那僵硬的对立和单纯被对立者的联结似乎可以去掉；那些神奇的作为是人做出的，他和神性的东西似乎不可分离。
但联结越紧密，而这联结终究不会成为结合，被联结起来的对立者那种不自然就越刺眼。
